decision.summary: Tenant wants to replace the landlord's broken LG washer with their own, which stays theirs. That needs landlord consent rather than a repair job. I asked the landlord for consent, who pays for removal and fitting, and what happens to the LG. I told the tenant, added a note, and set a follow-up for 29 July.

args.decision_needed: The tenant reports the LG washing machine (here when they moved in) has a power failure and, from their own web search, can't be fixed. They offer to buy a replacement at their own cost; it would remain their property, not be on the inventory, and they would take it when they leave. Please confirm: (1) do you consent to the tenant fitting their own machine; (2) who pays to disconnect and remove the existing LG and fit the new one; (3) what should happen to the existing LG (we inspect/repair, dispose, or other). Alternatively we can send our contractor to inspect it first.
options: Consent to tenant's own machine; state who pays for removal/fitting and what happens to the LG
Send our contractor to inspect/repair the LG first

Because the current machine belongs to the landlord, fitting your own needs their consent, so we have put your offer to them, including that the new one would stay yours and go with you when you leave. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code. We will update you by 29 July.
